summary: Iteration 11 validates the /api/health.mongo.host redaction fix and the Atlas connection. 23/23 pytest assertions PASS against https://recharge-hub-184.preview.emergentagent.com. /api/health.mongo.host returns 'atlas-purple-ball.wvr7dp7.mongodb.net' with no '@' character (password stripped) and no 'localhost'. env.MONGO_URL_set is true. Full Atlas flow verified end-to-end: admin login (200, role=admin), wrong password 401, POST /api/users creates fresh retailer (itest_retailer_<hex>@example.com, prefixed for easy cleanup), POST /api/wallet/transfer credits 500.00, retailer login succeeds, POST /api/recharge (mobile_prepaid/airtel/100) returns success with commission_rate=0.02 and commission=2.00, transaction persists in /api/transactions and the retailer ledger contains recharge + commission + transfer_in rows. Regression: /api/wallet/ledger, /api/operators, /api/reports/summary, /api/commissions all 200 with admin token. Static source-code guards verified: server.py contains _MONGO_URL_MISSING flag derived from `'MONGO_URL' not in os.environ`, the startup 'Mongo config → host=...' log with the NOT-SET warning branch, the login 500 hint 'MONGO_URL env var is not set on this deployment' guarded by a 'localhost:27017' substring check, and the health endpoint host redaction via split('@'). Reset-scenario (missing MONGO_URL restart) skipped as requested since it would require supervisor changes.

minor.issue: The redaction in /api/health only strips creds via `split('@')[-1].split('/')[0]`. If the connection string ever omits '@' (e.g. some SRV strings without user:pass) the code falls back to `mongo_url.replace('mongodb://', '').split('/')[0]` — this branch is NOT covered by tests because our Atlas URL always has '@'. Non-blocking, but consider adding a test with a credential-less mongodb://host:27017 URI to lock the behavior.
PytestRemovedIn10Warning still present on the module `src` fixture inside TestServerSourceGuards (instance-method class-scoped). Purely cosmetic; test passes.

Legacy @app.on_event('startup')/'shutdown') handlers still coexist with the lifespan context manager (both call _ensure_admin_seeded). Idempotent so harmless, but the on_event decorators are deprecated in newer Starlette. (Repeat of iteration-9/10.)

action_items: USER ACTION (out of code scope): the reported 500-on-login is happening on the user's Vercel deployment because MONGO_URL / DB_NAME are NOT set in Vercel environment variables. The user must add MONGO_URL (pointing at their Atlas cluster with a properly URL-encoded password) + DB_NAME=rechargepro + JWT_SECRET + ADMIN_EMAIL + ADMIN_PASSWORD in the Vercel project settings, ensure Atlas Network Access allowlists 0.0.0.0/0 (or Vercel egress IPs), then redeploy. After redeploy, GET /api/health on the Vercel URL must show env.MONGO_URL_set=true, mongo.ok=true, mongo.host=<atlas-hostname>, and admin_seeded=true.
OPTIONAL: remove the legacy @app.on_event handlers now that lifespan covers indexing + seeding + client.close(). Cleans up DeprecationWarning.
OPTIONAL: add a unit test for the credential-less MONGO_URL redaction branch (mongodb://host:port with no user:pass).
critical_code_review_comments: The `mongo.host` field is computed twice — once at module init (`_mongo_host_safe`, used only in the startup log) and again inline inside the /api/health handler using the same split logic. Extract into a helper `_safe_mongo_host(url)` and reuse; avoids drift if one is later changed and the other isn't.

The 500 body hint appended by the login handler (`Database error: {type}. MONGO_URL env var is not set on this deployment... Check /api/health for full diagnostics.`) is informative but leaks the exception class name to the client. Fine for an internal debug deploy; on a public Vercel URL this reveals slightly more than necessary. Consider making the class name log-only and keeping only the hint + pointer to /api/health in the client response.

The self-heal resync inside _ensure_admin_seeded (overwrites password_hash from env if verify_password fails) still surprises operators who rotate the admin password via /api/me — the very next login will overwrite that rotation with ADMIN_PASSWORD from env. Consider gating this behind an env flag (ADMIN_PASSWORD_ENFORCE=1) OR only resyncing when password_hash is empty / not a bcrypt hash (starts with $2). (Repeat from iterations 9/10.)

server.py is now 905 lines — approaching the 700-line-split guideline. A refactor into routers/auth.py, routers/wallet.py, routers/recharge.py, routers/reports.py + a services module would keep future changes isolated.
requests library imported as _http (line 639) is used synchronously inside async /api/auth/session — blocks the event loop for up to 10s. Should be httpx.AsyncClient. Pre-existing.

logger is initialized AFTER _ensure_admin_seeded is defined but referenced inside it. Only bites at import time (never called from module scope during import), but a future refactor could break this. Move logging.basicConfig()+getLogger() above the seed function.

Any mongosh-based tests from iteration 10 (test_health_and_login_resilience.py) will still target local mongodb://localhost:27017/test_database and are therefore SKIPPABLE / STALE relative to the live backend. rca_of_the_issue: User bug: 'localhost:27017: [Errno 111] Connection refused' 500 on Vercel login. Root cause is deployment configuration, not code — MONGO_URL env var is missing on the Vercel service so the module-level fallback (mongodb://localhost:27017) kicks in and Vercel has no local Mongo. This iteration adds three diagnostic surfaces to make the failure mode obvious: (1) module-level `_MONGO_URL_MISSING` flag + startup log line `Mongo config → host=... env_MONGO_URL_set=<bool>` and a WARNING branch when the env is missing — verified present in source; (2) /api/health.mongo.host returns the actual redacted target host so operators can see immediately whether the process is pointed at Atlas or fell back to localhost — verified live: preview shows 'atlas-purple-ball.wvr7dp7.mongodb.net'; (3) login handler now appends 'MONGO_URL env var is not set on this deployment — set it to your MongoDB Atlas connection string and redeploy.' to the 500 body when the exception mentions localhost:27017 — verified in source. Actual fix (setting env vars on Vercel) is out-of-scope for this container; the user must do that on their Vercel dashboard and redeploy.
